question.text: Which of the following statements about the AMFI Registration Number (ARN) is correct?

answer.text: ARN is issued by SEBI directly to all mutual fund distributors
ARN is a lifetime registration that never requires renewal
ARN is allotted by AMFI after the distributor completes NISM certification (or the applicable CPE/exempt route) and KYD, and both ARN registration and the NISM certification must be renewed on time
ARN is issued separately by each AMC whose schemes the distributor wants to sell

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.121-p.122), AMFI allots the ARN to a distributor after the distributor obtains the NISM Series V-A certification (or, for exempt categories, completes the applicable CPE route) and complies with the Know Your Distributor (KYD) requirements. Employees of distributors separately obtain an EUIN from AMFI. The ARN identifies the distributor across all AMCs. The Trap: Option A is wrong — SEBI is the regulator, but AMFI issues the ARN. Option B is wrong — both the NISM certification and the AMFI registration must be renewed on time (p.310). Option D is wrong — the ARN is a single, centrally issued number used across AMCs; it is not issued AMC-by-AMC. Note: The CPE/exempt path is recognised in the source for specified categories who are not required to clear the certification examination afresh; both certification and AMFI registration carry an ongoing renewal obligation.
